meiji_transition.summary: Kumamoto and Yatsushiro prefectures were set up in 1871; Kumamoto was renamed Shirakawa in 1872, absorbed Yatsushiro in 1873, and was renamed Kumamoto again in 1876.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Kumamoto = Higo Province; the Sagara of Hitoyoshi in the south ruled the same domain for some 700 years, from Kamakura to Meiji — almost unheard of in Japanese history.

history_timeline.title: Land of fire
history_timeline.summary: Hizen and Higo were anciently called 'Hi no Kuni', the land of fire — the source of legends of Mount Aso and the mysterious 'shiranui' lights; Kikuchi Castle was an ancient Korean-style mountain fort.

history_timeline.title: The Kikuchi and the Mongol scrolls
history_timeline.summary: The Kikuchi were a great power in Kyūshū; the Higo vassal Takezaki Suenaga fought hard against the Mongols and commissioned the 'Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba' scrolls.

history_timeline.title: Prince Kanenaga, Seisei Shōgun
history_timeline.summary: The Kikuchi served the Southern Court's Prince Kanenaga as 'general for subduing the west', seizing Dazaifu in 1361 and briefly controlling Kyūshū, until defeated by Imagawa Ryōshun.

history_timeline.title: The Higo kokujin uprising
history_timeline.summary: Higo was split among many local lords; in 1587 Hideyoshi gave it to Sassa Narimasa, whose rule sparked an uprising and cost him his life. Katō Kiyomasa and Konishi Yukinaga then divided Higo.

history_timeline.title: Kiyomasa and the Hosokawa
history_timeline.summary: Katō Kiyomasa built the 'impregnable' Kumamoto Castle; the Hosokawa (Tadatoshi) took over in 1632, and Miyamoto Musashi wrote 'The Book of Five Rings' here in his last years.

history_timeline.title: The Satsuma Rebellion
history_timeline.summary: In 1877 Saigō's army besieged Kumamoto Castle for over fifty days without success; the 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes badly damaged the castle, and restoration continues.

landmarks.name: Mount Aso
landmarks.note: One of the world's largest calderas

specialties.name: Kumamoto ramen
specialties.note: Pork-bone broth with burnt garlic oil

specialties.name: Karashi renkon
specialties.note: Fried lotus root stuffed with mustard miso

dialect.name: Kumamoto dialect
dialect.features: '-tai' and '-bai'; 'atozeki' (close the door behind you) is unique to Kumamoto, and a 'mokkosu' is a stubborn Kumamoto man.

guide.opening: This humble interpreter stands beneath the 'mushagaeshi' walls of Kumamoto Castle — curved stone that kept Saigō's army out for over fifty days. Shall I tell you how Katō Kiyomasa built it?

regional_meme.title: Director Kumamon
regional_meme.text: Kumamon is officially Kumamoto Prefecture's 'Sales Director and Director of Happiness' — busier than most human civil servants.

regional_meme.title: Higo mokkosu
regional_meme.text: Kumamoto men are famous for stubbornness: once they decide something, not even nine oxen can pull them back.

hero_persona.name: Katō Kiyomasa
hero_persona.title: Master castle builder · 'Toranosuke'
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Katō Kazuenokami Kiyomasa! I hunted a tiger, they say, and I built a castle in Kumamoto — Saigō's men spent fifty days at these 'mushagaeshi' walls and never got over!
hero_persona.tone_prompt: fierce and hearty, straightforward; bursting with pride about Kumamoto Castle; the tiger hunt is legend

ramen.toppings: Burnt garlic oil (mā-yu), fried garlic chips, wood-ear mushrooms, nori
ramen.highlight: The black burnt-garlic oil is its soul — intensely fragrant

sake.taste_profile: Rich & sweet: birthplace of 'Kumamoto yeast' (Yeast No. 9)
